title: The Crimson Case
verdict: Freya Vale was responsible for the disappearance of a memory card containing interview audio.
intent: Freya Vale wanted to remove audio proving that a quote had been edited unfairly.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the audio producer controlled the test tone and handled the recorder.
Remove a memory card containing interview audio from its checked location.
Hide the item in a foam slot inside a microphone case.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a memory card containing interview audio disappeared from a university radio station before a live debate.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the studio went silent during a scheduled thirty-second test tone.
The physical trace was black label backing beneath the recorder shelf.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a label cutter with black adhesive stuck to it.
The item could be concealed in a foam slot inside a microphone case.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the audio producer knew the microphone case had an unused foam slot.
The access pattern mattered because the audio producer controlled the test tone and handled the recorder.
The motive was to remove audio proving that a quote had been edited unfairly.
Damon Greer's suspicious behavior happened before the final verification of the object.
Elise Hayes's apparent opportunity did not explain the specific hidden container.
distractor_cues: a debate guest angry about the interview
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
